findings.title: §5.2 item (2) blocked-on-adopter-conflict value description (plan-doc line 119) omits the 'with meaningful content' qualifier for TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> reference — inconsistent with invariant 2 line 47 + §6 024B line 190
findings.evidence: Plan-doc line 119 (§5.2 item (2), blocked-on-adopter-conflict value definition): 'blocked-on-adopter-conflict — invariant-10 conflict-close path; NO invocation occurred (conflict was discovered before invocation); a TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> TF is filed + referenced in DISPATCH-NOTE; the PR MUST NOT modify branch-protection-log.md (CI script asserts absence of modification per invariant 2).' The TF reference requirement reads 'filed + referenced in DISPATCH-NOTE' — no meaningful-content qualifier. Fix-round-4 added the meaningful-content requirement to invariant 2 line 47: 'MUST reference the filed TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> TF in DISPATCH-NOTE matching the standardised prefix with meaningful content (status field + non-empty description; bare-prefix stub fails CI per the same rule above)'. Fix-round-4 also added it to §6 024B line 190: 'for blocked-on-adopter-conflict: requires TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> reference with meaningful content'. §5.2 is the per-adopter onboarding contract — it is the PRIMARY reference that a cascade-slice author (024C–024F) reads to understand what a blocked-on-adopter-conflict close requires. A slice author following §5.2 alone would file a bare-prefix TF reference (no status field, no description) and believe they have satisfied the contract. That bare-prefix reference would fail the CI check specified in invariant 2 — but the slice author would not know this from §5.2. This is the same propagation-gap pattern: fix-round-4 added the requirement to the definitive spec site (invariant 2) and the acceptance-criterion site (§6 024B) but not to the contract-view site (§5.2). The gap is MAJ because: (a) §5.2 is the direct reading path for cascade-slice authors; (b) a CI failure at 024C/024D/024E/024F submission time caused by a missing meaningful-content requirement the author never knew about defeats the purpose of specifying the requirement in the plan-doc; (c) the pattern has now recurred four rounds in a row — fix-round-4 was already the propagation-gap fix, but it only propagated to three of four sites.
findings.recommendation: Update plan-doc §5.2 item (2) blocked-on-adopter-conflict value definition (line 119) to add the meaningful-content qualifier: replace 'a TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> TF is filed + referenced in DISPATCH-NOTE' with 'a TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> TF is filed + referenced in DISPATCH-NOTE with meaningful content (status field + non-empty description; bare-prefix stub fails CI per invariant 2)'. The sentence already carries the log-file-absence requirement; add the meaningful-content qualifier for the TF reference to match invariant 2 + §6 024B.

findings.evidence: Plan-doc line 208 (§7 risk surface, R-024-06 mitigation column, CI enforcement paragraph): 'check-invocation-log-entry.sh (a) verifies the TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> reference IS present in DISPATCH-NOTE AND (b) actively asserts that docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md was NOT modified in the PR diff.' Assertion (a) says only 'reference IS present' — no meaningful-content qualifier. Fix-round-4 added the meaningful-content requirement to invariant 2 line 47 ('with meaningful content (status field + non-empty description; bare-prefix stub fails CI per the same rule above)') and §6 024B line 190 ('for blocked-on-adopter-conflict: requires TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> reference with meaningful content'). R-024-06 is the risk-table row that Codex executors read when implementing check-invocation-log-entry.sh. R4-NEW-MAJ-001 (just closed) established that R-024-06 is a normative implementation-guidance anchor: when R-024-06 omits a requirement that invariant 2 specifies, a Codex executor implementing from R-024-06 alone builds the deficient version. Fix-round-4 fixed the negative-assertion gap in R-024-06 (adding '(b) actively asserts log file was NOT modified') but the same edit introduced a new gap: the TF-reference check (a) is now correctly described for the negative-assertion dimension but still omits the meaningful-content dimension. A Codex executor reading R-024-06 assertion (a) would implement a prefix-presence check only — the same stub-row bypass that R4-NEW-MAJ-002 (safety) closed for the onboarded-operator-bump path. The R-024-06 description of assertion (a) must be brought into conformance with invariant 2 + §6 024B.
findings.recommendation: Update plan-doc R-024-06 mitigation (line 208) to add the meaningful-content qualifier to assertion (a). Replace '(a) verifies the TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> reference IS present in DISPATCH-NOTE' with '(a) verifies the TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> reference IS present in DISPATCH-NOTE with meaningful content (status field + non-empty description; bare-prefix stub fails CI)'. The existing assertion (b) is correct and should not change. The closing sentence 'Both assertions are required; one positive + one negative' remains accurate (assertion (a) is positive + meaningful-content; assertion (b) is negative). Add the existing 'Closes 024A R4 R4-NEW-MAJ-001' marker appended with '+ 024A R5 R5-NEW-MAJ-002 (blocked-on-adopter-conflict TF meaningful-content propagation to R-024-06)' for traceability.

findings.title: DISPATCH-NOTE criterion (iii) describes invariant 2 as 'operator-run + invocation-logged' — a stale summary that no longer reflects invariant 2's primary normative content (three-value cascade-status CI enforcement spec with meaningful-content + negative-assertion requirements)
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE line 51, criterion (iii): '§2 names the 10 non-negotiable invariants — opt-in per-adopter, operator-run + invocation-logged, cascade does NOT touch existing adopter content (purely additive), FLA-independent, required-check primary + scorecard-emit secondary, no cross-repo write, per-adopter rollback, version-skew tolerance via post-bake observation, bus-factor-1 acknowledged, no backwards-incompatible adopter-side work.' The description of invariant 2 is 'operator-run + invocation-logged' — accurate at R1 time but now severely underselling the normative content of invariant 2. After four fix-rounds, invariant 2 is the plan-doc's central safety control: it specifies the three-value cascade-status field, all three CI check-paths with their positive evidence + meaningful-content + negative-assertion requirements. A reviewer using criterion (iii) as a checklist reads 'operator-run + invocation-logged' and confirms invariant 2 is named — but the summary gives no signal that they should specifically verify three-value coverage, per-path CI enforcement, and meaningful-content requirements. This is the same category as CMP-nit-003 (R2) which upgraded criterion (vi) to name §5.5; here criterion (iii) needs its invariant 2 description updated. The severity is MIN rather than nit because the cascade-status CI spec is the central safety control and criterion (iii) is the acceptance-checklist anchor for §2 — leaving it with a stale summary increases the probability that a future reviewer misses the three-value check.
findings.recommendation: Update DISPATCH-NOTE criterion (iii) to replace 'operator-run + invocation-logged' with 'operator-run + invocation-logged + cascade-status CI enforcement (three values: onboarded / onboarded-operator-bump / blocked-on-adopter-conflict; per-path positive + meaningful-content + negative-assertion requirements per invariant 2)'. The full invariants list in criterion (iii) does not need to be expanded — this targeted update to the invariant 2 description is sufficient to signal to future reviewers that they should verify the three-value spec completeness, not just that §2 exists.

pattern_observation: This is now the fifth round in which a fix applied to invariant 2 + §6 024B was not propagated to all four normative sites that describe the same CI check-path (invariant 2, §5.2, §6 024B, R-024-06/R-024-07). The complete set of sites for the blocked-on-adopter-conflict TF reference requirement is: invariant 2 (definitive spec), §5.2 item (2) (contract-view for slice authors), §6 024B (acceptance criterion for 024B implementer), R-024-06 (implementation-guidance for Codex executors). Any new requirement added to invariant 2 for a cascade-status check-path must be propagated to all four sites simultaneously. Fix-round-5 should enumerate all four sites for each of the three cascade-status paths and verify each requirement (positive evidence, meaningful content, negative assertion) appears at all applicable sites before submitting for R6. If fix-round-5 propagates R5-NEW-MAJ-001 and R5-NEW-MAJ-002 without introducing any new propagation gaps, R6 should reach fixpoint on this dimension.
